clue.text: Song about bounder in the Greek department

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the song's letters go round the bounder

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
a cad is a bounder, an ungentlemanly man

explanation.surface: Someone sings about a rotter somewhere in the Greek section.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is a mountainous administrative region of the Peloponnese in Greece.

clue.text: Cited dictator in supplement

indicators.note: in means the dictator's title sits inside the word for supplement

parts.note: to add is to supplement
Il Duce was the title of Mussolini, the Italian dictator

explanation.surface: A tyrant quoted in an appendix.
explanation.definitionFit: To adduce evidence is to bring it forward or cite it as proof.

clue.text: Dress in which hems can go crooked

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of line, so the letters of hems can go are twisted

explanation.surface: A garment whose hems may end up uneven.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheongsam is a close-fitting Chinese dress with a high collar and slit skirt.

clue.text: Area where soil's deposited as flower comes out

definitions.text: Area where soil's deposited as flower comes out

parts.words: Area where soil's deposited as flower comes out
parts.note: flower means something that flows, a river, and the soil is silt laid down at its mouth

explanation.surface: A garden bed where earth is heaped as blooms emerge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword trick: one that flows, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment builds a triangular landform at a river mouth.

clue.text: Compound cleans air of poison

indicators.note: compound means mix, so the letters of cleans air are mixed up

explanation.surface: A chemical that purifies the atmosphere of toxins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' looks like the chemical definition but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Containing arsenic, a famous toxin, describes a substance of that poison.

clue.text: Panel with French frozen scene

parts.note: a panel of experts, like a table, is a group seated together; table also means a flat board
French au (as in café au lait) means with

explanation.surface: A discussion panel with a French member produces a scene frozen in time.
explanation.walkthrough: AU is French 'to the', but in dish names like café au lait it reads as 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau vivant is a group of motionless actors posed as a picture.

clue.text: Part of plant that's underground, right?

parts.note: the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: A question about whether a plant part grows below the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is an example: a swollen storage stem or root.

clue.text: Canned fruit for first meeting arranged

parts.note: canned is slang for drunk, as is blind
a date is the fruit of a palm

explanation.surface: Tinned fruit is served at an introductory meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic outing set up between strangers who have never met.

clue.text: Start — head off for the middle of America

indicators.note: head off means remove the first letter

parts.note: Americans spell centre as center

explanation.surface: A traveller sets off for the heartland of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter into something is to begin it, as an actor's entrance starts a role.

clue.text: Rebel force occupying ancient city

indicators.note: occupying means the force sits inside the ancient city

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
to prise is to force open

explanation.surface: Rebels' troops take over an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rises up against authority is an insurgent.

clue.text: Hang out in back of beyond by water-hole

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so take the end of beyond

parts.note: a well is a hole dug for water

explanation.surface: Someone lives out in the outback next to a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang out somewhere, informally, is to live or stay there.

clue.text: She produces silly stories full of banal sentimentality, primarily

definitions.text: She produces silly stories full of banal sentimentality, primarily

indicators.note: full of means the anagram surrounds the letters that follow
silly suggests the letters of stories are messed about into a new order
primarily means take the first letter of each of banal and sentimentality

explanation.surface: A description of a journalist churning out mawkish tear-jerking stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges STORIES into SOISTER, and 'full of' puts B and S, the initials picked by 'primarily', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob sister is a journalist, traditionally a woman, who writes sentimental human-interest stories.

clue.text: Goods carrier on certain trips

indicators.note: trips means stumbles, so the letters of on certain fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Freight is shipped on particular journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' reads as journeys, which suits goods, but it is a verb telling the letters of ON CERTAIN to stumble into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipping container is a large box used to carry freight.

clue.text: Game shoots

explanation.surface: A pub game, or someone firing.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is a pub game of throwing missiles at a board; darts also means moves suddenly or shoots, as a glance does.

clue.text: Records here discounted — 50% off

indicators.note: 50% off, in this shopping surface, means keep only the first half of the word discounted

explanation.surface: A record shop advertises half-price sales.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a club where records are played for dancing.

clue.text: Rude solos in mess, without any humming

indicators.note: in mess means the letters of rude solos are jumbled

explanation.surface: Coarse solo performances in an army mess hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humming' here means smelling bad, British slang, not a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Humming is British slang for stinking, so lacking any smell fits.

clue.text: One of a group of solicitors working at cross purposes?

definitions.text: One of a group of solicitors working at cross purposes?

parts.words: One of a group of solicitors working at cross purposes?
parts.note: solicitors here are not lawyers but people soliciting votes, and the cross purposes are the crosses voters put on ballot papers

explanation.surface: A law firm whose partners undermine each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Solicitors suggests British lawyers; it means people who solicit votes door to door, whose purpose is the voter's X.
explanation.definitionFit: A party worker going door to door to ask for votes is the person meant.

clue.text: The Statesman magazine?

parts.note: a statesman read as a man from a certain US state gives the name of a magazine, echoing the New Statesman

explanation.surface: A request for the political weekly the New Statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Statesman is a British political weekly; here a 'statesman' is a resident of the Empire State.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous American weekly magazine named after a resident of that state.

clue.text: Stayed at home to cultivate daughter's ornamental tree

parts.note: sat in means stayed at home rather than going out
to woo is to cultivate someone's favour

explanation.surface: A homebody grows a decorative tree for their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical tree yielding glossy yellow timber used in fine furniture.

clue.text: Usual decree for such a partner? On the contrary

definitions.text: for such a partner? On the contrary

explanation.surface: A rule asked of a partner, with a contrarian twist.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'usual decree' is customary law; 'On the contrary' flips the second part: it is not a decree for such a partner but the kind of partner, a common-law wife or husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Customary law built on precedent is ordinary, unwritten law; a cohabiting unmarried spouse is called a partner of this kind.

clue.text: Great work in Derby, for example

explanation.surface: A masterpiece produced in the city of Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is one of the five Classics, Britain's top flat horse races.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterpiece of lasting quality is so called; Britain's flagship horse races are also named that.

clue.text: One not a hit as minor actor

explanation.surface: A failed stage performer who never landed a hit play.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat, such as a wide or a bye.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket run that does not come from hitting the ball is so called, as is a film walk-on performer.

clue.text: One gives prompt assistance as car's held up by copper, note

indicators.note: held up by means, in a down clue, the car sits above the copper

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A motorist's vehicle is stopped by a policeman, who issues a ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen showing a presenter's script helps them remember lines.

clue.text: A warning concerning doctors put about

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

indicators.note: put about means turned round, so the word for concerning is written backwards

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A caution regarding medics spread around by rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A warning' looks like the whole definition, but A is wordplay; 'put about' applies only to the word for concerning, giving ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The amber traffic light is the caution signal between green and red.

clue.text: Head old party

parts.note: bean is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A veteran party leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is British slang for a lively celebration or spree.

clue.text: Leguminous plant with powdered head

parts.note: something ground is crushed to powder
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A bean plant that has a dusty top.
explanation.definitionFit: The peanut plant is a legume whose pods ripen below the soil.

clue.text: Such dignity, when old, is standard

explanation.surface: Elderly dignity becomes the norm.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Glory is the nickname of the US flag, a standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour or majesty is great honour; the second sense is the US flag nickname.

clue.text: Is detective using sense, and informers?

explanation.surface: A detective relies on good sense and tip-offs.
explanation.walkthrough: Nose is slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sniffing out clues means snooping; nark-type tipsters are slang informers.

clue.text: Routine preparations one in suit finds a chore

parts.note: a spade is a card in the suit of spades
work is a chore, labour

explanation.surface: A man in a business suit finds daily tasks tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in suit' suggests an office worker but means a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundwork done before the main task is the hard, dull preliminary labour.

clue.text: Uncomplaining, so admits to being a philosopher

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the word for so takes in the second piece

parts.note: Latin sic means so or thus
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone without grievance confesses to being a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being a philosopher' is a second, looser definition: a follower of Zeno's school.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone enduring hardship without complaint is called philosophical in this way.

clue.text: Like some tyres, not soft in disagreeable way

indicators.note: not soft means remove P, the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

parts.note: cross-ply tyres have cords laid diagonally across each other

explanation.surface: Some tyres, being hard, behave unpleasantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting irritably or bad-temperedly is acting in an annoyed manner.

clue.text: What's left in 9, containing uranium

indicators.note: containing means the word for live holds the next letter

parts.note: the answer to 9 across means live, which is reside
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Leftovers at a dwelling, with uranium inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Remaining material after a process is the leftover matter.
